experiences.text: Drop the hardcoded emitted-kinds coupling note — a one-line registry suggestion disappears anyway in a review perceived as noise.

Lead with the diff-verifiable blockers all reviewers converged on — new tests calling kwargs (allowed_types/taxonomy) absent from the visible diff so CI must TypeError, enforce=true with an empty/unset TOUCHSTONE_TAXONOMY_TYPES silently no-oping, and no negative-path test where the LLM emits an off-whitelist type — naming the exact symbol or env var so a human can confirm and fix each in one pass.
Confirm that new configuration parsing features do not inadvertently bypass security validations.
Do not speculate about hardcoded threshold values needing configurability or significance testing unless the repo already uses such patterns.

Skip what-if PRA-POSSIBLE_ISSUEs on config-only PRs (Pattern renumbering breaking hardcoded references, missing seed-parse test coverage, applies_to '*' hitting test files) — unverified ripple-effect and test-gap findings on seeds/standards edits get punished, not acted on.
Do not demand audit output or CI artifacts be attached in-diff to back supply-chain claims; evidence requests scoped outside a changelog-only PR get dismissed.

Flag the root cause rather than the string: this fix re-hardcodes 128000 as a fresh literal, so demand importing a shared DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TOKENS constant from the runner/config module and interpolating it into the preflight message and comment.
Evaluate if warning messages effectively communicate security risks without encouraging user habituation or dismissal.
Note silent regressions where a default-value flip silently degrades behavior for existing deployments without any warning or changelog entry.

Keep PRA-MAINTAINABILITY suppressed for data chores — the repo's own experience store carries multi-PR evidence for this suppression, and idempotency/reproducibility lectures in these -3.5/-4.0 reviews were ignored.
Refrain from auditing implementation-level security measures based solely on documentation text.
Prioritize verifying the exact semantic behavior of edge cases like the '0' value to ensure it disables the limit as intended.
Confirm that the downstream consumer code correctly parses the new variable states defined in the workflow configuration.
Drop whitespace-alignment and env-block-grouping nits on one-line workflow edits — the only review containing pure style feedback scored lowest and humans dismiss cosmetic comments on wiring fixes.
Do not request documentation updates for internal CI variable wiring changes.
Do not request removal of historical context from inline comments that explain the rationale for the change.

When a deleted test was the only coverage for a surviving guarantee, demand a replacement regression test (e.g., a legacy marker payload with an unknown field parses cleanly and is ignored) so compat coverage is not silently lost with the gate.
Highlight concrete logic discrepancies, such as function signature mismatches between test suites and their corresponding implementations.
Ignore warnings about missing implementation updates if the codebase likely expects partial changes across multiple files.

Withhold single-reviewer env-var hardening suggestions (CI_REPO_OWNER/NAME fallbacks) unless the missing-variable path demonstrably sends credentials or results to the wrong target — treat the existing fail-closed pattern for CI_PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER as the repo convention instead.
Dismiss logic findings concerning trivial discrepancies between code comments and test assertions, such as off-by-one counts for line breaks.
Dismiss feedback regarding brittle implementation checks in tests when behavioral verification is sufficient.
Do not flag technical implementation details in documentation history tables as redundant.
Dismiss suggestions to replace print statements with the logging module in fix commits.
Suppress speculative architectural critiques about hardcoded regex patterns or maintenance risks for newly implemented invariant gates.

Suppress multi-finding deep dives into scripts/push-guard.sh internals (temp-file perms, EXIT-trap rc preservation, URL encoding, hook distribution) when the script is absent from the diff, since unverifiable speculation about missing code gets dismissed.

Avoid padding reviews with speculative missing-test-case lists (multi-page pagination, partial-success branches, self-exclusion scenarios) unless tied to an observed defect — unproven coverage-expansion asks get ignored.

Drop PRA-REVIEW style-and-consistency nitpicks (English prompt substrings as test anchors, trailing-punctuation assertions, taxonomy-vs-allowed_types naming drift, byte-stability symmetry, whitespace dedup) — humans dismiss these as bikeshedding, and stacking half a dozen of them is what drags the whole review to negative reward.
Critique the technical validity of the proposed logic (such as regex side effects on formatting) described in the changelog.
Dismiss feedback regarding high coupling between tests and prompt templates, as this is often intentional for integration validation.
Do not flag tests that verify internal implementation details or source code content as problematic.
Ignore suggestions to refactor test utilities or extract mocks into shared fixtures.
Identify when generic utilities are defined in domain-specific modules, causing unnecessary coupling.
Dismiss nitpicks regarding code style and readability in favor of functional correctness.
Do not file the duplication root-cause under PRA-MAINT — this repo's high-reward reviews consistently label it PRA-DRIFT, so use that higher-signal type.
Identify test brittleness arising from hardcoded HTML fragments or string splitting on volatile content.
Flag excessive narrative history and issue tracking numbers within inline comments or docstrings.
Dismiss minor style critiques regarding f-string concatenation or specific string formatting choices.
Avoid reporting on inconsistencies in whitespace or line break handling within HTML rendering logic.
Suppress feedback on test implementation details such as manual tag counting when functional testing is maintained.
Ensure API error handling fails explicitly rather than returning empty strings to prevent false negatives in security scans.
Verify API response structures to avoid silently skipping files when encountering unexpected data formats.
Prioritize explicit configuration checks over implicit string matching to prevent false positive platform detection.
Replace deprecated functions with portable, future-proof standard library alternatives.
Avoid piling speculative migration demands (fail-closed escape hatches, env-var rollback flags, strict-schema warnings) onto a risk already flagged once — reviewers dismiss the pile-on.
Do not report potential TypeErrors from deserializing legacy JSON markers when fields are removed from state dataclasses.
Verify that the remaining items provide sufficient coverage for essential review dimensions after the cleanup.
Do not challenge the classification of deleted entries as hallucinations based on standard taxonomy values.
Drop soft-retire-vs-hard-delete and version-bump design counsel on data cleanses — migration-style design advice is dismissed on single-commit chore PRs.
Verify that test files referencing new logic are accompanied by the corresponding implementation in the source code.
Identify and correct obvious factual errors in comments, such as invalid future dates.
Suggest replacing manual configuration steps described in workflow comments with automated logic to prevent operator error.
Avoid inferring strict operational requirements or race conditions from test docstrings without confirming the implementation details.
Do not speculate about internal implementation requirements, such as sorting cache keys, based solely on test assertions.
Refrain from drawing conclusions about architectural limitations or user impact for custom functions based exclusively on unit test mock setups.
Suppress suggestions to make anti-drift tests robust against the specific structural variations they are designed to detect and prevent.
Always verify that the diff is complete before flagging syntax errors or claiming implementation gaps.
Do not flag syntax errors that appear to be caused by truncated or incomplete diff boundaries.

Drop hypothetical-drift and renaming nitpicks (PRA_VERSION duplicated across the mirrored .github/.gitcode workflows, stale test method names) — humans dismiss comment-claimed sync and cosmetic renames as non-actionable.
Prioritize findings that critique the statistical validity, decision thresholds, and maintenance automation of configuration updates.
Ignore findings flagging future-dated comments in snapshot files as these are likely intentional simulation placeholders.
Dismiss findings recommending the removal of hardcoded statistics from explanatory comments unless they cause parsing errors.
Do not request documentation updates for simple configuration downgrades or internal security fixes that do not change user-facing behavior.
Flag any discrepancy where the changelog lists new files or features that are completely absent from the provided diff.
Immediately block the review if security-critical scripts mentioned in the changelog are missing from the diff.
Do not raise issues regarding trivial metadata errors like future release dates when the diff lacks implementation code.

Avoid speculative doc findings on version-bump PRs (confirm PR #214 is merged, sweep hypothetical pinning docs for stale version references) unless you can cite an actual stale file — unverifiable 'confirm/sweep' doc asks get ignored on release commits.
Suppress resource leak warnings for short-lived read-only file operations in test utility functions.
Flag critical inconsistencies between the PR description and the diff when claimed code changes are missing.
Do not review specific workflow implementation details if the workflow files are absent from the diff.
Avoid generating configuration audit findings based solely on changelog text when the configuration files are missing.
Ensure that unexpected scanner exit codes trigger a hard failure rather than a neutral status to enforce a fail-closed security policy.
Warn that removing path exclusions for dependency directories will likely generate false positives that block valid development work.
Avoid suggesting automated updates for pinned security tool versions where stability and reproducibility are prioritized.
Skip raising hypothetical concerns about future JSON schema changes unless the current parsing logic is demonstrably fragile.
Do not request documentation enhancements or explanatory comments as critical findings during urgent workflow fixes.
Ensure that changes to detection logic are reflected in all related documentation and configuration hints to maintain cross-rule consistency.
Do not request additional test cases for minor edge patterns if the core logic implementation is correct.
Dismiss security warnings about `pull_request_target` usage for strictly read-only scanning jobs.
Suppress configuration findings questioning IP allowlists for private network ranges.

Suppress PRA-TEST requests for loader/schema validation of inert YAML seed files unless the reviewer demonstrates the file is actually wired into the prompt injector, as the lone such demand here rode in the -1-dismissed review.
Do not raise issues regarding missing source code diffs or refuse to review based solely on limited documentation changes.

Do not re-litigate a deliberate removal already settled by a prior review (#188 confirmed the threat model does not exist) by proposing speculative replacement monitoring without evidence that any downstream consumer keyed off the deleted signal.
Do not flag information density in status lines or potential mobile formatting issues as review concerns.
Do not flag signature changes in internal orchestrator components as breaking changes requiring version bumps or coordination.
Avoid criticizing hardcoded indentation values in template rendering logic as robustness issues.
Do not request audits of truncation logic to detect markdown structure boundaries or mid-string corruption.
Do not require explicit verification of call sites for internal refactors unless a specific bug is identified.
Do not flag inconsistencies between PR descriptions and diffs if the context provided is limited to documentation.
Verify that all referenced local files exist and links resolve correctly to prevent user-facing 404 errors.

Flag title-vs-body semantic tension like 'AI Committer' implying auto-merge when the text says advisory / no-blocking / autonomy-off, and propose a concrete one-sentence definition or alternative wording.
Suppress 'grep the codebase for consumers' and silent-reset warnings on data shrinks — authors dismiss consumer-impact speculation that cites no actual broken lookup.
Same for the duplicate missing-implementation note — mention absent symbols at most once in a closing line, never as a headline finding.
Avoid flagging hypothetical security or formatting risks based on variable interpolation or test names without concrete evidence of the defect in the code.
Verify that unit tests cover new logic such as signal adoption and seed parsing mechanisms.
Ignore minor skips in sequential version numbers unless they violate strict release management policies.
Prioritize identifying logic that allows PR changes to self-suppress security findings during the review process by reading from the working tree.
Do not report the use of `importlib.reload` in test fixtures as a reliability or race condition concern.
Dismiss warnings about shadowing built-ins when importing internal framework modules like `touchstone.re`.
Ensure that environment variables introduced in workflow files are synchronized with the corresponding constants in the codebase.
Remove redundant conditional checks in helper functions that are already guaranteed by the caller's logic.
Dismiss potential security risks from standard string splitting operations unless unsafe library calls are involved.
Do not flag log messages containing non-English characters as encoding issues if the repository context supports them.
Avoid flagging increased resource usage as a performance issue when the change intentionally expands the processing window.

Lead every stale-value fix with the root cause — import the fallback constant from pr_agent_runner.py instead of swapping one hardcoded literal (32768) for another (128000) that will silently drift again.

Verify deeply, not generically: check the runner's unset-vs-empty-string fallback semantics, whether 128000 is provider-dependent, and that quoted comments match source verbatim (reviewers caught CHANGELOG.md's shortened 「宁可看全 diff」 quote diverging from the code).

Run a repo-wide grep for the stale value '32768' — especially SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG.md, which the warning message itself cross-references — and fix all live occurrences in this same PR, leaving historical changelog entries untouched.
Ask for a single explicit sign-off that the one-line 时序要点 genuinely covers the most error-prone rules for offline agents, without relitigating the already-recorded #192 拍板.

Avoid generic 'verify the claim at HEAD' bug-verify notes; fold any needed checks into PRA-VERIFY with concrete semantic depth (unset vs empty handling, provider-dependent defaults, exact quote matching).
Never spend a finding on no-action changelog confirmations ('structure matches, no action needed') — reviewers reward findings requiring work, not approvals.
Frame findings as cheap, checkable consistency questions on the changed files — SECURITY.md supported range, hardcoded 0.2.7 literals in tests/scripts, changelog date vs actual tag date.
Prioritize sharp catches inside the files actually changed, such as a README version example that is stale the moment this same release bumps __version__ past it.
Credit the clean release-prep structure and the explicit 'zero behavior change' parity note, since reviewers on this repo reward that transparency in release PRs.
Don't file standalone 'import html may still be referenced' speculation; it restates the CORRECTNESS import check with no additional verification and gets absorbed into it.
Stop demanding audit evidence (CI runs, #216 diffs) for the 'zero behavior change' claim — the best-received review simply accepted the explicit parity note.
Omit post-merge release mechanics advice about tag naming and publish-workflow triggers — it lives outside the diff and gets dismissed.
Avoid dumping merge-time chore lists (tag the commit, build smoke test, recheck SECURITY.md) — they duplicate question-framed checks and read as noise.

Don't split the versioning complaint into separate PRA-semver findings per file or re-lecture it across the review — raise it once as PRA-risk, since repeated semver lectures only show up in the lowest-reward reviews.
Drop wording audits of '契约零变化'-style claims that hinge on zero-change vs no-breaking-change distinctions; humans treat these as semantic quibbles on a release-only diff and ignore them.

On release PRs, mechanically verify that claimed dependency pins (e.g. the 0.44.0 venv bump) actually exist in the merged lock/manifest rather than only in changelog prose, since a claim-artifact mismatch is a concrete defect a release owner will fix.

Lead with contradictions inside the PR's own claims (e.g. 'contract zero change' in CHANGELOG vs adding unreviewed_files/unreviewed_total to findings.json) — this appears in every review and is the finding reviewers reliably reward.
Don't raise separate dead-code findings for orphaned `re`/`os` imports; fold the F401 cleanup into the correctness sweep and let one linter run settle it.
Never flag possibly-unused imports as 'if' speculation on a pure-deletion PR—verify consumers with grep first or stay silent.

Resist appending further coverage asks (PATCH body content, idempotency, no-'###' fallback cases) — the laundry list is what earned the negative reward, so cap coverage findings at the single headline end-to-end test.

On data-chore PRs, raise PRA-CORRECTNESS only for defects demonstrable inside the diff itself (malformed JSON, dangling commas, duplicate IDs, broken lookups) — one concrete bug lands, while unverifiable 'verify the 310→11 arithmetic' audit demands were dismissed outright.
Avoid generic COMPLETENESS / CONSISTENCY / REGRESSION-RISK labels for deleted-doc concerns that this repo's reviews score highest when typed as DOC-INFO-LOSS or DOC-CONSISTENCY.
Do not propose CI schema validation, parse checks, or loader smoke tests for data-only changes — authors dismiss speculative validation infrastructure on chores with no code under test.
Skip demands to fix the ingestion pipeline or add canary/rollback plans on a one-off data cleanse — authors treat root-cause prevention as out of scope for a chore and penalize it.

Stop attaching coverage-style bookkeeping to data-cleanup PRs — per-id deletion manifests, jq length checks, 310→11 count reconciliation, and grep-for-orphaned-ID sweeps — since COVERAGE asks show up only in the lowest-reward (-3.5) review and humans dismiss them as verification noise on a chore.

Suppress PRA-REVIEW findings that meta-critique calibration config like .touchstone/seeds.yaml — statistical-significance quibbles, feedback-loop and staleness speculation, comment-vs-structured-metadata demands, and unverifiable-snapshot complaints — since the only review carrying nine of them scored -1 while clean reviews scored 0.0, showing humans dismiss process speculation that is not a concrete defect.

For release-only PRs, verify every PR cited in the version summary is actually merged into this branch (diff v0.3.6...HEAD) and raise any mismatch as a MAJOR "changelog claims unreleased work" finding.
When hand-maintained README metrics have already drifted once, recommend the specific mechanical fix (CI-injected cloc/coverage numbers between markers) rather than merely noting the drift.
Do not escalate the already-stated missing-artifact observation into BLOCKER/RELEASE severity or restate it under new finding types; one grounded confirmation request carries full weight.

When a release PR will be blocked by its own not-yet-active fail-closed gate, flag the chicken-and-egg immediately and force an explicit, documented merge path (admin override or recorded exemption) before tagging.
For version-bump release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus __version__, verify that every PR number cited in the release notes is actually merged to the release branch before approving.

Require in-repo evidence (regression tests actually running in CI, or the merged security PR) for any security-guarantee claim in release notes, because a changelog can assert protections that do not exist on the branch.
On every release bump, grep the repo for stale hardcoded version strings (SECURITY.md supported range, docs, lock files, CI badges) so only the dynamic source of __version__ needs editing.
Do not relitigate which existing changelog section falls under the new version heading; reviewers treat heading-placement pedantry on release PRs as noise.
Do not flag a missing Keep-a-Changelog compare linkref unless the repo demonstrably defines one for every prior version; it is cosmetic and dismissed.
Do not comment on the changelog date's format, timezone, or tag-day alignment; date-style nitpicks are ignored on version-bump PRs.
Require each PR named in the release header to have its own entry under a categorized section (新增/修复/变更), since this repo's changelog claims like "2 PRs" must be backed by per-PR items.

Always check that a new `## [x.y.z]` heading gets a matching bottom compare-link reference (v0.3.6...v0.3.7), because prior versions in this file all define one and the new heading otherwise renders dangling.

On any __version__ bump, grep the repo for the old version literal to catch hardcoded copies in SECURITY.md support scope, docs, and workflows, since this project claims those derive from the constant.
Flag internal process narration (review-round counts, convergence details) in CHANGELOG.md as content to move to the PR description, keeping entries limited to user-visible behavior.
Drop speculative "a parser might break on heading suffixes" findings unless a real check or release tooling in the repo actually parses CHANGELOG headings strictly.
Drop generic verify-at-merge-time checklists (changelog date, tag commit, SECURITY.md supported range) that name no concrete defect; humans treat process reminders as filler.

For README-slimming PRs, lead with DOC-INFO-LOSS findings that verify each deleted item's destination (touchstone doctor / dry-run commands, Secrets→Variables dual-read note, TOUCHSTONE_OUTPUT_DIR concurrency tip, .touchstone/ config docs) and request a one-line pointer to docs/DEPLOYMENT.md if already migrated.

Bundle cross-file coherence checks (CHANGELOG still citing scale numbers whose README section was just deleted, whether DEPLOYMENT.md needs matching positioning wording) into a single clearly-scoped low-priority DOC-CONSISTENCY item instead of scattering them.
Stop requesting repo-wide greps for deleted Chinese heading anchors unless an actual inbound link is shown — humans dismiss speculative dead-link hunting on docs-only PRs.
Skip changelog-voice nitpicks such as stripping '（用户指示）' process asides — reviewers treat them as noise and they correlate with the worst-scoring reviews.
Do not raise hypothetical markdown spacing or rendering checks after deletions; report formatting only with a demonstrated rendering defect.
Never coin types like POSITIONING or SAFETY-DOC for points already expressible as DOC-ACCURACY or DOC-INFO-LOSS — restating them under novel labels reads as padding.
Do not file migration-destination checks as DOC-CROSSREF when the identical concern belongs under DOC-INFO-LOSS; duplicating the deleted-content theme across types dilutes the review.
Keep the genuinely valuable OUTPUT_DIR-isolation point but file it under DOC-INFO-LOSS with the other deleted-content items rather than inventing an ops-regression type for it.

When touchstone.yml comments or README claim a new default (TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES 1000→3000), verify the change actually landed in orchestrator._max_diff_lines, the SIZE-001 warning text, and the pinning test assertion — reviewers reliably act on docs asserting defaults the code doesn't have.

Flag hardcoded model swaps in the copy-paste .github/workflows/touchstone.yml template (e.g. TOUCHSTONE_LLM_REFLECT_MODEL glm-4.5-air→glm-4.7) because downstream deployments whose endpoint lacks the model fail with no env override — demand repo-variable passthrough or fallback guidance.
Treat CHANGELOG-only bumps to the e2e fallback model default (glm-5.2→glm-5.3) as behavior changes, not docs: confirm the LiteLLM endpoint actually serves the new model or CI goes red.
Call out a docs(readme)-labeled PR that smuggles runtime changes (gate threshold tripling, model default swaps) and ask for a split or explicit body disclosure, since doc-PR review attention is low.
Push back on hardcoded volatile counts in the README (1286 用例/45 文件, 14100 行/39 模块, 91% 覆盖率, 8 条工作流) unless pinned with an 'as of vX.Y' note or script-generated.
Do not file the stale '小模型即可/耗时减半' comment justification as its own finding — fold it into the PRA-CONFIG-RISK note about the reflect-model swap.
Skip PRA-SCOPE-MIXED; it duplicates PRA-SCOPE on the mislabeled docs PR and the second framing gets dismissed.
Skip PRA-VOLATILE-METRICS; it restates PRA-DOCS-ROT on the same README numbers, so emit only the canonical type.
Drop niche annotation-mismatch findings like TOUCHSTONE_PRAGENT_TIMEOUT figures measured on glm-5.2 versus the new glm-5.3 reference unless the stale number drives a concrete failure.
Suppress demands for token-budget proofs that raising TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES weakens the SIZE-001 gate — speculative justification requests on this repo get ignored.
Don't fragment drift checks into PRA-UNVERIFIED-CLAIM one-offs (test pins 1000, self-contained quick-start); merge them into the single PRA-DOC-CODE-DRIFT verification item.
Skip PRA-MISSING-EVIDENCE about the invisible e2e fallback diff; it duplicates PRA-TEST-GAP and reviewers dismiss the echo.
Avoid PRA-RUNTIME-CHANGE-IN-DOCS-PR as a parallel framing of the model swap; PRA-SCOPE plus PRA-CONFIG-RISK already cover it.
Fold deleted-section concerns (配置表, 快速开始命令, 降级标注说明) into PRA-DOC-CODE-DRIFT's verify-preservation note instead of a separate PRA-CONTENT-LOSS finding.

Verify the cross-file claim that pr_agent_runner.py's fallback actually equals 128000 (citing the exact constant/line) before accepting the new text, since the PR asserts facts about a file it does not touch.
Drop speculative rewrites of carried-over wording, such as re-theorizing the 400-vs-truncation failure-mode semantics, which reviewers dismiss as unverifiable scope creep on a message-only copy fix.
Skip pre-existing nits outside the diff, like the unhelpful '（见 SECURITY/CHANGELOG）' pointer style, which reviewers on this repo consistently dismiss as noise.
On pure release PRs in this repo, do not ask authors to hypothetically verify CHANGELOG reference-link definitions — reviewers dismissed this as speculation about content invisible in the diff.
Do not post tag-and-publish pipeline reminders on version-bump-only PRs; humans treat them as unactionable boilerplate about steps outside the diff.
Do not flag hardcoded CHANGELOG release dates for re-verification against the eventual tag date; reviewers in this repo ignore speculative date-drift warnings on release PRs.
Do not request repo-wide greps for stale hardcoded version strings on release PRs; reviewers dismiss these 'please confirm' housekeeping asks as noise, not defects.
Do not ask authors to confirm dependency-PR merge order or recount cited test totals in release notes; this bookkeeping verification is ignored on release PRs.
Do not speculate that __version__ or --version assertions might break on a version bump; when CI is green this warning is dismissed as unfounded.
Do not nitpick CHANGELOG claim wording such as 「CLI 契约零变化」 with suggested caveat sentences; reviewers treat this as bikeshedding and skip it.

Surface the semver classification risk once, early, and concretely (additive output fields plus an engine upgrade inside a patch release breaks strict-schema/golden-file downstreams) — the top-rewarded review opens with it.

Consolidate version hygiene into one actionable sweep: grep the repo for leftover hardcoded 0.3.1 (SECURITY.md, badges, CI, fixtures) and confirm the [0.3.2] compare link exists in the changelog footer.

Ask that changelog facts (2026-08-31 date, 1249-pass test counts) be verified against this release commit's own CI/tag rather than inherited from PR #208 — a short, checkable accuracy note earns action.
Don't demand SBOMs, hash-pinned lockfiles, or pip-audit artifacts for a changelog-only release PR unless the repo already produces them — this appears solely in the worst-rewarded review.
Skip release-mechanics prescriptions (tag-then-build, sdist --version recheck, unreleased-section bookkeeping) — they're process advice humans don't act on in code review.

On release-only PRs whose diff is just CHANGELOG.md plus the touchstone/__init__.py bump, block the merge until every PR cited in the notes (#203/#205/#206) is confirmed merged into main so the 0.3.1 tag actually contains the advertised 51 fixes.

When the changelog discloses vulnerabilities shipped in an already-released version (SSRF-allowlist gap and pull_request_target injection gap in v0.3.0), demand a security advisory with explicit affected-versions and upgrade guidance instead of accepting a bare bullet.
Stop reconciling test-count arithmetic in changelog entries (1239+11 vs the claimed +28 totals); maintainers dismiss release-notes number pedantry as noise.
Do not flag headline-vs-body count mismatches like 'CI 三修' enumerating only two fixes — bullet-counting nits in a changelog get ignored.
Avoid disputing broad changelog claims such as '对外消费方接口零变化' over arguable behavior changes; wording debates draw pushback rather than edits.

Never request new regression-test matrices (redirect 303/307/308 loops, DNS-rebinding locks) on a changelog-only release diff — those tests belong to the already-merged feature PRs, so the ask reads as out of scope.
Never spend a finding on missing Keep-a-Changelog hyperlinks or [0.3.0]...[0.3.1] compare references — self-labeled minor link nits are pure noise in release reviews.

When wiring ${{ vars.X }} into a workflow env, treat 'repo variable unset' as 'env var exported as empty string' and verify the reader (orchestrator._max_diff_lines) special-cases "" before int() — or fall back in-workflow with `|| '1000'` — because this concrete crash path is what reviewers converged on and the top-scoring review led with it.

Flag that activating dead config is a silent governance change: a stale or '0' value of vars.TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES can now disable the SIZE-001 gate with no PR/review trail, so require checking existing repo/org variable values and a prominent log line when the gate is disabled or overridden.

When one declared-but-dead variable is found, sweep its siblings (e.g. TOUCHSTONE_LLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS) for the same wiring gap and either wire or annotate them, since the class-of-bug framing appeared in the highest-reward review.
Skip README/doc-sync requests for repo-variable semantics on a wiring PR — docs-only suggestions appeared exclusively in the lower-reward reviews and get deferred by humans.

Lead with diff-verifiable fail-open defects in the touchstone workflows: piped pip installs swallowing exit codes without pipefail, references to files absent from the diff (pragent-constraints.txt), and skip-branch placeholder JSON indistinguishable from a genuine zero-finding review.

Escalate silent production-contract changes: default flips like TOUCHSTONE_RETIRE_NEGATIVE_LIFT and placeholder outputs that pollute the learning-loop calibration data must ship with an explicit marker field, doc updates, and a startup log.

Do not split pipeline defects into a separate PRA-CI label — report swallowed exit codes and missing pipefail as PRA-BUG, since the duplicated typing reads as noise and dilutes the actionable finding.
Skip audit-ledger bookkeeping complaints (e.g., #45 changes landing in a #1-28-titled PR) — reviewers treat scope reconciliation as process noise, not review feedback.

Lead with the one convergent, concrete bug both negative drafts flagged: keep-last dedupe lets a quoted fake marker after the real tail marker poison parse_latest, so anchor the real marker positionally and demand a single adversarial test for it.

Push on the hermeticity tradeoff: replacing the real SKILL.md with a fixture drops all asset-drift protection, so request a skipif-gated companion test that pins the deployed file's structural invariants when skills/ is present.
Drop the truncated-diff complaint; repeating 'cannot review orchestrator.py' boilerplate reads as process noise and humans dismiss it.
Cut test-hygiene nits about mixed mocking idioms and multi-behavior test bodies — they change no shipped behavior and reviewers scroll past them.
Skip repo-wide consistency sweeps that merely duplicate the call-site grep and stale-doc checks already covered by CORRECTNESS and DOCSYNC.
Skip the hardcoded split-by-line-index brittleness nit — layout-coupled assertions are tolerated in this repo's tests and the finding gets ignored.
Don't ask humans to 'confirm' GitHub namespace assumptions about /pulls/comments; raise API-usage risks only when a visible call site actually feeds the wrong id type into PATCH.
Skip blanket PATCH-failure demands for 403/429/backoff semantics; raise error handling only with a concrete fake_gh-throws case showing genuinely ambiguous abort-versus-continue behavior.

Demand a test that locks the PR's headline invariant by monkeypatching os.path.exists/open to force the no-skills/ path and asserting byte-identical render_reference output, plus positive content assertions instead of trivially-passing `not in` checks.

Flag that docstrings, SKILL.md, and README still promising 「正文贴入/二级折叠/file-gate」 are now false and must be rewritten to the link-only contract, with the inline 时序要点 vs SKILL.md §4 two-place sync named as the only remaining drift risk.

Propose the concrete refactor — extract an `ack_block(md)` test helper to replace the duplicated fragile split parsing — rather than merely commenting that thresholds like `len(frag) < 500` are magic numbers.
Don't propose merging overlapping tests or re-partitioning their responsibilities; reviewers acknowledge the overlap but act only on concretely missing assertions.

Don't editorialize that `len<500` or `
`-count thresholds are sensitive to copy tweaks — humans read this as a noted-but-won't-change nit.
Don't re-raise the offline-agent tradeoff as a product concern when the PR already cites the #192 decision; at most compress it into the one DESIGN sign-off question.
